page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor containing 32 physical cores running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, supported by 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Compute capabilities include hardware-level support for Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 instruction extensions for accelerated vector and matrix workloads.

Hardware tradeoffs include the absence of integrated local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, meaning non-volatile disk persistence requires external Azure Premium Storage attachments. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth, delivering 430.32 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 185.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Multi-core performance tests reflect upper-quartile results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,795.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 77,248.44, whereas single-core stress-ng throughput remains in the median range.

The dense RAM configuration and high memory bandwidth provide qualitative resource efficiency for memory-bound systems by minimizing node fragmentation. The E64s_v6 demonstrated 36,080.41 operations on PassMark database tests, 89.49 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, and 91.27 GB/sec static web throughput. These characteristics position the instance for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed key-value caches, data transformations, and CPU-driven batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 64-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. Operating with 32 physical cores at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 512.0 GB of RAM alongside 260 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 instruction sets. It includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring remote Premium Storage for data persistence. Benchmark results highlight top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 430.32 GB/sec read and 185.29 GB/sec write throughput on large blocks, as well as top-decile Geekbench multi-core execution and PassMark database operations. While single-thread execution aligns with standard industry medians, multi-threaded capacity and high memory per core enable efficient consolidation. The E64s_v6 is aligned with memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as distributed in-memory databases, caching systems, analytics processing, and batch compilation.
